stem: The electronic health record becomes unexpectedly unavailable during the shift. Which nursing action best supports safe continuity of care?

options.A: Activate the facility's approved downtime procedure and use the designated backup documentation/order process, such as approved paper forms
options.B: Stop documenting client care until the electronic system is restored
options.C: Rely on memory and recreate all assessments and medication-related documentation after the system returns
options.D: Create an informal personal documentation system that is not part of the facility's downtime plan

rationale: Current federal Health IT SAFER guidance emphasizes contingency planning for planned and unplanned EHR unavailability. HealthIT.gov specifically notes that practices should have a well-designed backup process, including paper-based documentation and ordering when the EHR is unavailable. Therefore the nurse should follow the facility's approved downtime procedure rather than delay documentation, rely on memory, or improvise an unauthorized record system.
educational_objective: Use the facility's established EHR downtime process to maintain safe, continuous documentation and care during electronic-system outages.
source_organization: Office of the National Coordinator for Health Information Technology (ONC), HealthIT.gov
source_document_title: SAFER Guides — Contingency Planning; Health IT Playbook — Quality & Patient Safety
source_version_date: SAFER resources updated 2026; current pages accessed 2026-08-17
source_locator: SAFER Guide: Contingency Planning — planned/unplanned EHR unavailability; Health IT Playbook, Quality & Patient Safety: recommended well-designed paper-based system for documenting activities and ordering medications/tests/procedures when EHR is unavailable
source_claim_supported: Health care organizations should have established contingency procedures for EHR downtime, including backup documentation/order processes such as paper-based systems.
blueprint_source_organization: National Council of State Boards of Nursing (NCSBN)
blueprint_locator: Management of Care — Information Technology, printed p.22 / PDF p.26: utilize information technology resources, enter documentation accurately/completely/timely, and use resources to promote quality client care
blueprint_topic: Management of Care — Information Technology / EHR downtime contingency
correction_summary: Replaced the private HIMSS source with current federal ONC/HealthIT SAFER guidance. Framed paper documentation as an example of the facility-approved backup process rather than a universal stand-alone rule and eliminated unsafe memory-based reconstruction.
audit_findings: A aligns with current federal contingency-planning guidance. B creates a documentation gap; C risks inaccurate reconstruction; D bypasses approved health-information processes. One best answer remains without assuming every organization's exact downtime workflow is identical.
